style.vernacular: Compact harbour capital on a grid, rebuilt after fires (1805, 1813, above all 1948) so the centre is mostly 1-4 storey concrete and render shops and offices in pastel paint with corrugated-iron roofs, with older timber-and-fretwork Caribbean houses on the hillsides; steep green volcanic hills (Morne Fortune) behind, banana and palm farmland and rainforest inland.
style.ornament: Eastern Caribbean vernacular: verandahs and galleries with timber fretwork (gingerbread) trim, jalousie shutters, steep corrugated roofs in red or green, contrasting pastel window and door surrounds; Catholic churches with plain arched openings. Typical-colour palette is general Eastern Caribbean practice, not a measured survey.

sources.what: grid layout on reclaimed flood plain, rebuilt after fires in 1805, 1813 and 1948, harbour, landmarks (cathedral, Derek Walcott Square, library, market, Government House)
mountainous volcanic island, tropical climate, Roman Catholic majority, English/French Creole, banana economy
